porbos.title: The Call to Settle Badr’s Account • A Dream, a Counsel • Three Hundred Turned Back on the Road • Those Whose Help Was Not Accepted • Fifty on the Mountain • The Right of the Sword • Hamzah’s Spear, Wahshi’s Spear • The One Whom the Angels Washed • The Pass Left Empty

blocks.0: The Call to Settle Badr’s Account
blocks.1: At Badr seventy of Makkah died. Seventy went to Madinah as captives. In every house of Makkah there was now an empty place. Some had no father, some no brother, some no son. Abu Sufyan’s caravan had returned safely, and the profit of that trade was lying deposited in Makkah. ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Rabi‘ah, ‘Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl and Safwan ibn Umayyah went to Abu Sufyan and the other owners of the caravan. They said, Muhammad has killed our best. With this wealth help us fight him, perhaps we can take revenge. They agreed. The call spread. The Ahabish, Kinanah and the tribes of Tihamah joined too.{{1}}
blocks.2: One was Abu ‘Izzah. A poet. He had been captured at Badr, and the Prophet {{1}} had shown him mercy and released him. He was poor, the father of many daughters. Safwan said to him, help us with your poetry. Abu ‘Izzah said, Muhammad has been kind to me. Safwan said, if you return I will take responsibility for your daughters, and if you die they will live with my daughters. He went. He went around from tribe to tribe, reciting poetry.{{2}}
blocks.3: Another had a task. Jubayr ibn Mut‘im had an Abyssinian slave, Wahshi. Expert at throwing the spear, almost never missing. Jubayr said, if you kill Muhammad’s uncle Hamzah (RA) and take revenge for my uncle Tu‘aymah, you are free. Quraysh set out with three thousand, with two hundred horses. Some women went along, so that the fighters would not think of fleeing. With Abu Sufyan was Hind bint ‘Utbah, whose father and brother had died at Badr. When she passed by Wahshi, Hind would say, Abu Dasmah, calm our insides, and calm yourself too.{{1}}
blocks.4: Badr had broken their hands. From a broken hand hatred spreads, and stubbornness too. That stubbornness became capital, became an army, became song. When revenge falls into a merchant’s hand it becomes investment capital. In our homes too, pouring money into lawsuits and old quarrels, years go by. But an investment whose very name is hatred never yields a profit.
blocks.6: Quraysh came and camped near Uhud. News reached Madinah. That night the Prophet {{1}} saw a dream.
blocks.8: I saw in a dream that I shook a sword, and its tip broke off. That was the loss the believers suffered on the day of Uhud. Then I shook it again, and it became better than before. That was the victory Allah brought and the gathering of the believers. And I saw cattle there too, and whatever Allah does is good; those cattle were the believers on the day of Uhud.{{1}}
blocks.9: The dream also had a strong coat of mail. That coat of mail was Madinah. And cattle being slaughtered. Those cattle were some of the Companions.{{1}}
blocks.10: So his view was to fight staying in Madinah. Let the women and children go to the fortresses, the fighting will be in the lanes, arrows shot from the rooftops. Madinah had by then blocked up its lanes and made them a fortress. ‘Abdullah ibn Ubayy’s view was the same. But many of the Companions, who had not been able to be at Badr, wanted to go out and fight. The honour of Badr had slipped from their hands, so they were restless for another chance. Hamzah (RA) said, by the One who sent down the Book upon you, we will fight them, and we will not sit in Madinah. Nu‘aym ibn Malik (RA) said, Prophet of Allah, do not deprive us of Paradise. By the One in whose hand is my soul, I will enter Paradise. The Prophet {{1}} said, by what strength? He said, I love Allah and His Messenger, and I will not flee from the battlefield. The Prophet {{2}} said, you have spoken the truth. He was martyred that very day.{{3}}
blocks.11: The middle of the month of Shawwal, a Friday. The Prophet {{1}} prayed the Jumu‘ah prayer, gave counsel, told them to be patient. That very day a man of Banu al-Najjar, Malik ibn ‘Amr (RA), had died. The Prophet {{2}} first prayed his funeral prayer. Then he went into his house and put on his coat of mail. Now many of the Companions realized the Prophet’s {{3}} view was actually to stay. They said, O Messenger of Allah, if you wish, we will stay. The Prophet {{4}} said, it is not fitting for a prophet, after he has put on his coat of mail, before Allah has decided between him and the enemy, to take it off.{{5}}
blocks.12: Counsel was sought. Differing views came. The Prophet {{1}} set aside his own view and accepted the view of many. Then once the decision was made, there was no question of going back. In our homes too there is counsel. But after a decision is made we become of two kinds. Some keep lamenting, I did say so. Some, having given a differing view in the counsel, take it as a personal insult. After the counsel of Uhud, there was no disagreement left among the Companions. What the Prophet {{2}} decided became everyone’s.
blocks.14: (O Prophet! Recall that time of the Battle of Uhud) when in the morning you went out from your home to position the believers at their posts for battle. And Allah hears everything and knows everything.{{1}}
blocks.15: Three Hundred Turned Back on the Road
blocks.16: With a thousand Companions the Prophet {{1}} set out from Madinah, taking the road called Badi‘. Ibn Umm Maktum (RA) was left in charge of prayer in Madinah. Reaching a place called al-Shawt, between Uhud and Madinah, ‘Abdullah ibn Ubayy stopped. He said, Muhammad did not listen to me, he listened to those boys. Why should we get ourselves killed? He turned back with three hundred men. After them went ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr ibn Haram (RA), the father of Jabir (RA). He said, do not leave your people and the Prophet in front of the enemy. They said, if we knew there would be fighting, we would not have turned back. ‘Abdullah said, may Allah keep you away, enemies of Allah. Allah will make His Prophet independent of you.{{2}}
blocks.17: On one side, the Companions then had two views. One group said, fight them, they are hypocrites. The other group said, no.
blocks.19: When the Prophet {{1}} set out for Uhud, some of those who had set out with him turned back. The Companions became two groups. One group said, we will fight them. The other said, we will not fight. Then it was revealed: ‘What is the matter with you that you have become two groups concerning the hypocrites?’{{2}}
blocks.20: Within the army two tribes also grew weak. Banu Salimah and Banu Harithah. The thought of turning back came to them too. Allah held them firm.
blocks.22: Two groups among you were thinking that they had lost heart. Yet Allah was their guardian and helper. The believers should rely on Allah alone.{{1}}
blocks.23: This verse is about those two tribes. Jabir (RA) used to say, it was revealed about us. And I would not want it not to have been revealed, because Allah said in it, ‘Allah is their guardian’.{{1}}
blocks.24: Jabir (RA) was happy even though he knew his own weakness was recorded in the Qur’an. Because in the same verse Allah’s guardianship is also recorded. We want to hide our mistakes. For those whose mistakes too are written in history, beside their mistakes the announcement of Allah’s forgiveness is also written. However much we may break down on one day, for the one whose guardian is Allah, that is not the last word.
blocks.25: Those Whose Help Was Not Accepted
blocks.26: The Prophet {{1}} was going around looking over the soldiers of the camp. There were some boys, who were young in age. One of them was ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar (RA), who later used to say himself,
blocks.28: The Messenger of Allah {{1}} presented me for fighting on the day of Uhud. I was fourteen then. He did not permit me. On the day of al-Khandaq he presented me. I was fifteen then. He permitted me.{{2}}
blocks.29: With him others also went back: Usamah ibn Zayd, Zayd ibn Thabit, al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib (RA), Usayd ibn Zuhayr, ‘Arabah ibn Aws. They too had to go back. Rafi‘ ibn Khadij was also small. But he could shoot arrows, so he got permission. Samurah ibn Jundub was small, and was being left out. He said, I can beat Rafi‘ in wrestling. A wrestling match took place. Samurah won. He too got permission.{{1}}
blocks.30: The Ansar tribes of Madinah were bound by treaty with the Jews. They asked the Prophet {{1}}, shall we call our allies the Jews for help? The Prophet {{2}} said, we have no need of them.{{3}}
blocks.31: Yet that day one of the Jews entered the fight. Mukhayriq. A Jew of Banu Tha‘labah. He said, O Jews, you know that helping Muhammad is your duty. They said, but today is Saturday. He said, you have no Saturday. He took his sword and weapons and said, if I am killed, all my wealth belongs to Muhammad, he may do with it as he wishes. Then he went to the field and died fighting. The Prophet {{1}} said, Mukhayriq is the best of the Jews. His seven gardens the Prophet {{2}} made a waqf in the way of Allah. The first waqf of Madinah.{{3}}
blocks.32: The help of the one who was a believer was not needed. And the one who was of another religion suddenly offered his own chest. Whose side a person is really on, in the end that is recognized on the battlefield. Not by looking at the label.
blocks.34: Seven hundred Companions reached near Uhud. Ahead a high mountain, below it a flat field. On the other side the Quraysh army stood in rows. The Prophet {{1}} arranged the troops with their backs to the mountain, so that no one could attack from behind. He told the soldiers, no one will begin the fight unless I say so. Right behind the Muslim army was a mountain pass. Through that very pass the enemy’s horsemen could come and pounce from behind. Fifty archers were stationed there. Their leader was ‘Abdullah ibn Jubayr (RA).
blocks.36: The Messenger of Allah {{1}} stationed a group of archers and appointed ‘Abdullah as their commander over them. He said, do not leave your place. If you see us victorious over the enemy, still do not leave your place. And if you see them victorious over us, even then do not come to help us.{{2}}
blocks.37: Not even if we win, not even if we lose. Whatever happens, this place must not be left. The Prophet {{1}} gave the banner into the hand of Mus‘ab ibn ‘Umayr (RA). He put on two coats of mail. On the other side, on the right wing of Quraysh’s horsemen was Khalid ibn al-Walid, on the left ‘Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl.{{2}}
blocks.39: Taking a sword in his hand the Prophet {{1}} called out.
blocks.41: The Messenger of Allah {{1}} took a sword on the day of Uhud. He said, who will take this from my hand? Everyone stretched out their hands. Each was saying, I, I. He said, who will take it with its right? Then everyone held back. Simak ibn Kharashah Abu Dujanah (RA) said, I will take it with its right. He took it and with it split open the heads of the polytheists.{{2}}
blocks.42: Every hand reached out. But hearing ‘its right’ everyone stopped. Because right means duty. Asking for a sword is easy. Bearing its duty is hard. What is that right? In Ibn Ishaq’s narration, the Prophet {{1}} said, strike the enemy with it until it bends. Abu Dujanah (RA) tied a red band on his head, which, when worn, everyone knew meant today he had made up his mind to die. With the band tied he began to strut proudly between the two lines. The Prophet {{2}} saw him and said, this walk is disliked by Allah, but not in a place like this today.{{3}}
blocks.43: Al-Zubayr ibn al-‘Awwam (RA) felt a little hurt. The Prophet {{1}} had not given it to his cousin, but had given it to Abu Dujanah (RA). He decided, I will see what he does with this sword. He saw that Abu Dujanah (RA) was cutting down whoever he found. One polytheist was finishing off the wounded. Abu Dujanah (RA) went in front of him and finished him. Then he raised the sword over the head of a woman. That was Hind. The sword did not come down. He drew back. He said, I will not use the sword of the Messenger of Allah on a woman. Al-Zubayr (RA) says, I understood, Allah and His Messenger know best.{{2}}
blocks.44: The one who received power first asked, what is its right? We want power, we want position, we want a car, we want a house. Each has a right that comes with it. In front of whom to draw a line, when to stop the hand. And Abu Dujanah (RA) recognized, right in the middle of valour, where the sword must be lowered. Even in front of one woman of the enemy.
blocks.46: The fight began. The Muslims began to advance. Hamzah ibn ‘Abd al-Muttalib (RA) plunged like lightning into the disbelievers. ‘Uthman, son of the standard-bearer Talhah ibn Abi Talhah, fell into his hands. Then more standard-bearers. Siba‘ ibn ‘Abd al-‘Uzza came out. Hamzah (RA) said to him, are you opposing Allah and His Messenger? Then he struck, and Siba‘ was wiped out like yesterday. But behind a rock Wahshi was waiting then.
blocks.48: I was the slave of Jubayr ibn Mut‘im. At Badr Hamzah (RA) had killed Tu‘aymah. So Jubayr said to me, if you kill Hamzah (RA) and take revenge for my uncle, you are free. ... I hid for Hamzah (RA) under a rock. When he came near I threw my spear. The spear went in below his navel and came out between his two hips. That was my last meeting with him.{{1}}
blocks.49: The lion was finished. The one who knew no fear, a slave brought him down from behind. Hamzah (RA) was martyred. The Prophet’s {{1}} uncle, his milk-brother.{{2}}
blocks.50: That Wahshi returned to Makkah and was freed. Then Makkah was conquered, he fled to Ta’if. When the delegation of Ta’if decided to go to the Prophet {{1}}, he had nowhere left to go. Someone said, he does not kill anyone who accepts Islam.
blocks.52: I went and stood before the Messenger of Allah {{1}}. He saw me and said, are you Wahshi? I said, yes. He said, did you kill Hamzah (RA)? I said, it was as the news that reached you says. He said, can you keep your face hidden from me? I went out.{{2}}
blocks.53: In the shade of Islam Wahshi (RA) was spared. But the Prophet {{1}} did not want to see his face in front of him. Forgiving someone is one thing. Sitting with a smiling face while seeing their face in front of you is another. The Prophet {{2}} kept the difference between the two. He accepted Islam, and did not hide the wound in his own chest. Some forgiveness takes place in the heart but does not climb into the house. Slowly that too becomes easy. Knowing how to give oneself that time is another greatness of a person. There was another chapter in Wahshi’s life. After the passing of the Prophet {{3}}, Musaylimah the Liar emerged. Wahshi (RA) said, I will go out, perhaps by killing him I can make amends for the killing of Hamzah (RA). In the Battle of Yamamah he threw that same spear. Musaylimah died. An Ansari had also struck with his sword.{{4}}
blocks.54: Wahshi (RA) later used to say, I killed the best of people, and also the worst. Our sins do not leave us. But if someone truly returns, Allah’s door is open for them too.
blocks.55: The One Whom the Angels Washed
blocks.56: That day another had entered among the polytheists. Hanzalah ibn Abi ‘Amir (RA). His father was Abu ‘Amir al-Rahib. In the Jahiliyyah everyone called him the monk, because of his worship. But when Islam came he did not recognize the truth, did not want to recognize it. The Prophet {{1}} gave him the name, the sinner. He had left Madinah and gone off with Quraysh. And the son stood with the Prophet {{2}}. Hanzalah (RA) went straight toward Abu Sufyan. He threw him to the ground, raised his sword. Then Shaddad ibn Aws saw that. He struck. Hanzalah was martyred. After the battle the Prophet {{3}} said, the angels are washing your companion. Go to his wife and ask what the matter is. His wife said, as soon as the call to battle reached his ears, he went out. At that time he was in a state of impurity. The Prophet {{4}} said, that is why the angels washed him.{{5}}
blocks.57: His name remained, Ghasil al-Mala’ikah. The one whom the angels washed. The morning after the wedding night. A new wife at home. Yet leaving on hearing the call. So quickly that even the time for a bath was not taken. When a call comes to us, what do we do? Hearing the adhan we sit, saying there is work. Hanzalah’s hand held a wedding morning. Before one call Hanzalah kept no reckoning. The angels washed him.
blocks.59: The first part of the fight belonged to the Muslims. The polytheists began to flee. Al-Zubayr ibn al-‘Awwam (RA) says, I saw Hind and her companion women running with their shanks bared. Spoils of war were coming into the Muslims’ hands. The tents, weapons, camels left behind by the fleeing enemy. Then the archers standing on the mountain looked on.
blocks.61: When we met them, they fled, until I saw the women running up the mountain, they had lifted their garments from their shanks, their anklets showing. Then the archers began to say, the spoils, the spoils! ‘Abdullah said, the Prophet {{1}} took a pledge from me, that you would not leave your place. They refused. When they refused, their faces were turned away, and seventy were killed.{{2}}
blocks.62: Except ‘Abdullah ibn Jubayr (RA) and a few others, almost all went down. Their argument was, the Prophet {{1}} had said it for that time, for as long as the fighting was going on. The fight had already been won. Did the Prophet’s {{2}} command really have any word about time? The command was, even if you see us winning, do not leave. Khalid ibn al-Walid saw the mountain pass empty. He circled around and came up over it. ‘Abdullah and a few of his companions fought to the end and were martyred.{{3}}
blocks.63: What happened next turned the joy of victory into terror in a moment. Horsemen from above, the fugitives came back from the front. The Muslims were surrounded on both sides. Just then someone cried out.
blocks.65: On the day of Uhud the polytheists were defeated. Then Iblis cried out, servants of Allah, behind you! So the front group came back and began fighting the group behind. Hudhayfah (RA) saw his father Yaman (RA). He said, servants of Allah, my father, my father! ‘A’ishah (RA) says, by Allah, they did not stop, they killed him. Hudhayfah (RA) said, may Allah forgive you. ‘Urwah says, by Allah, a goodness remained in Hudhayfah (RA) until death.{{1}}
blocks.66: Yaman (RA) and Thabit ibn Waqash (RA) were very old. So they had been left in the fortress with the women. But hearing of the fight they said, only a little of our life remains, let us go. They came down into the battle. They fell on the wrong side. Thabit was killed by the polytheists. Yaman (RA) was killed by Muslims themselves, by mistake. What did Hudhayfah (RA) say? He said, may Allah forgive you. He even gave away his father’s blood money as a charity to the Muslims.{{1}}
blocks.67: The mistake happened at the wrong time. The one whose father died forgave in that very moment. When someone’s mistake harms us we remember it for years. Hudhayfah (RA) did not remember. And how small the archers’ mistake was when it began! One argument: the command was actually tied to time. The command had not changed, our interpretation had. The command that goes against my liking, for that we search the hardest for interpretations.

quiz.q: What was the Prophet’s ﷺ own view in the consultation?
o: To go to Uhud and fight
To station the archers on the mountain

quiz.q: After the consultation the Prophet ﷺ put on his coat of mail and then did not change his view. Why?
o: The enemy’s horsemen had been sighted
It is not fitting for a prophet to take off a coat of mail once he has put it on
The archers had already taken their places

quiz.q: Between Uhud and Madinah, where did ‘Abdullah ibn Ubayy stop?
With how many men did ‘Abdullah ibn Ubayy turn back?
Who was left in charge of prayer in Madinah?
Which two tribes had grown weak?
At what age was Ibn ‘Umar (RA) turned back on the day of Uhud?
How many archers were stationed at the pass, and who was their commander?
In whose hand was the Muslims’ banner placed?
In which battle did Wahshi (RA), who later accepted Islam, kill Musaylimah?

o: The Prophet ﷺ did not accept Wahshi’s Islam
Even after forgiveness, seeing the face brings back the grief for the beloved uncle

quiz.q: Seeing the one who hurt you brings the pain back. From the Prophet’s ﷺ words about Wahshi, what do you learn?
o: After forgiveness, mixing socially is obligatory
Forgiveness and easy mixing are different things

quiz.q: What was the Jahiliyyah title of Hanzalah’s (RA) father, and the name the Prophet ﷺ gave him?
In the dars’s analysis, where is the weakness in the argument the archers gave for leaving their place?

porbos.title: The Blood of the Prophet ﷺ • The Prophet ﷺ Has Died • Those Who Did Not Back Away • A Call From the Mountaintop • Cut Noses, Cut Ears

blocks.0: The Blood of the Prophet ﷺ
blocks.1: The ranks of the Muslim army broke. The polytheists, seizing the chance, advanced straight toward the Prophet {{1}}. They surrounded him. A stone thrown by ‘Utbah ibn Abi Waqqas broke one of the Prophet’s {{2}} lower front teeth on the right side, and his lower lip was torn. ‘Abdullah ibn Shihab split his forehead. Ibn Qami’ah struck his cheek. Two rings of the helmet sank into his cheek. Abu ‘Amir the sinner had secretly dug pits to make the Muslims fall. The Prophet {{3}} fell into one of his pits.{{4}}
blocks.3: The front tooth of the Messenger of Allah {{1}} was broken on the day of Uhud, and his head was cut. He was wiping his blood and saying, how will a people prosper who have split the head of their Prophet and broken his tooth while he is calling them to Allah? Then Allah revealed, ‘You have no authority’.{{2}}
blocks.4: This very verse is from that day.
blocks.6: (O Prophet!) You have no authority to decide in this matter whether Allah will accept their repentance or punish them, since they are wrongdoers.{{1}}
blocks.7: The Prophet {{1}} used to rise from bowing in the last rak‘ah of Fajr and invoke a curse on some by name. Safwan ibn Umayyah, Suhayl ibn ‘Amr, al-Harith ibn Hisham. Then it was revealed: you have no authority. The burden of judgment is Allah’s. Not even the Prophet’s {{2}}. One day Ibn Mas‘ud (RA) saw the Prophet {{3}} speaking of a prophet before him, whom his people had beaten until he bled.
blocks.9: It is as if I am looking at the Messenger of Allah {{1}}. He is speaking of one of the prophets, whom his people beat, and he is wiping blood from his mouth and saying, my Lord, forgive my people, for they do not know.{{2}}
blocks.10: Those who have hurt us, what do we say about them at that moment? The prophet he was speaking of had a prayer of forgiveness on his lips. The Prophet’s {{1}} own state was the same.{{2}}
blocks.11: The one wiping blood and saying, they do not know. Do we even give anyone the chance to say ‘they do not know’? Fatimah (RA) came. She began washing her father’s wound. ‘Ali (RA) was pouring water from a shield.
blocks.13: Fatimah (RA) was washing the wound of the Messenger of Allah {{1}}, and ‘Ali (RA) was pouring water with a shield. When Fatimah (RA) saw that the pouring of water only increased the blood, she took a piece of a mat and burned it. Then she applied that ash to the wound. The bleeding stopped.{{2}}
blocks.14: Seeing her father wounded and torn, the daughter did whatever she found at hand. The ash of a mat. In the time of injury, the person who helps most may be one near at hand. Whose wound-washing did not need any great arrangement.
blocks.16: Ibn Qami’ah cried out, I have killed Muhammad! Satan also cried out, Muhammad is killed! One group of the Muslims broke down. Some ran toward Madinah. Some climbed up the mountain. Some sat down, throwing away their weapons. In this crowd one man stepped forward. Anas ibn al-Nadr (RA).
blocks.18: My uncle, after whom I was named, was not at Badr. It was very hard on him. He said, the first battle of the Messenger of Allah {{1}}, I was not there. If Allah lets me later witness a battle with the Messenger of Allah {{2}}, Allah will see what I do. The day of Uhud came. ... He met Sa‘d ibn Mu‘adh (RA) in front. He said, Abu ‘Amr, where? I can smell the fragrance of Paradise from beyond Uhud. Then he fought until he was martyred. More than eighty wounds were found on his body: of sword, spear, arrow. His sister recognized him by the tips of his fingers.{{3}}
blocks.19: ‘Umar (RA) and Talhah (RA) were then sitting with the others, hands dropped. Anas (RA) said, why are you sitting? They said, the Messenger of Allah {{1}} has died. He said, what will you do living after him? Get up, die for what he died for. Then he plunged into the enemy.{{2}}
blocks.20: Among those who were at the back that day, for one of them the real question was not whether the Prophet {{1}} was alive or not. The question was, how much was he willing to give for the religion he had given. The news of the Prophet’s {{2}} death was false. But Anas ibn al-Nadr’s (RA) answer was such that, even had the news been true, it would not have changed. And exactly this is what the Qur’an said that day.
blocks.22: And Muhammad (may Allah’s peace and blessings be upon him) is only a messenger! Many messengers have passed away before him. If he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels? Whoever turns back on his heels will never harm Allah in the least. And Allah will reward those who are grateful.{{1}}
blocks.23: On the day of the Prophet’s {{1}} passing Abu Bakr (RA) recited this very verse. It seemed to the people as if they had never heard the verse before.{{2}}
blocks.24: A religion that exists because of a leader ends with the leader. A religion whose owner is Allah stays intact even when the leader is gone. In our homes too, in someone’s absence prayer, recitation, du‘a grow slack. It was going on because father was there, because mother was there, because the elder brother was there. Anas ibn al-Nadr (RA) said that day, I was here for him; I will remain for his religion.
blocks.25: Those Who Did Not Back Away
blocks.26: All around, collapse. But a few stayed at the Prophet’s {{1}} side. The enemy surrounded them. The Prophet {{2}} called out.
blocks.28: The Messenger of Allah {{1}} was separated on the day of Uhud with seven men of the Ansar and two of Quraysh. When they closed in on him, he said, who will turn them away from us? For him is Paradise, or he is my companion in Paradise. A man of the Ansar stepped forward, fought until he was martyred. Again they closed in. He said the same. In this way seven men of the Ansar were martyred. The Messenger of Allah {{2}} said to his two companions, we have not been fair to our companions.{{3}}
blocks.29: Seven. One by one. Each time the same call, each time the same answer. And each time another stood up, Talhah ibn ‘Ubaydillah (RA). He was saying, I, O Messenger of Allah. The Prophet {{1}} was saying, you stay, Talhah (RA). In the end, when no one else was left, Talhah (RA) fought.{{2}}
blocks.30: Years passed, yet that hand never became active again. Qays ibn Abi Hazim used to say later,
blocks.32: I saw Talhah’s (RA) hand, it had gone limp. It was with this hand that he protected the Prophet {{1}} on the day of Uhud.{{2}}
blocks.33: An arrow came and struck his finger. He said, ouch. The Prophet {{1}} said, had you said ‘Bismillah’, the angels would have lifted you up, and people would have looked on. The Prophet {{2}} himself was in two heavy coats of mail, tired from blow after blow. In front was a rock. He could not climb up. Talhah (RA) sat down. The Prophet {{3}} placed his foot on him and stood up on the rock.
blocks.35: The Prophet {{1}} had two coats of mail on the day of Uhud. He tried to rise toward the rock, but could not. Then he made Talhah (RA) sit down beneath, climbed on him, and stood straight on the rock. I heard the Prophet {{2}} say, ‘Talhah (RA) has made it obligatory (Paradise)’.{{3}}
blocks.36: Whenever Abu Bakr (RA) brought up Uhud, he would say, that day was entirely Talhah’s (RA).{{1}}
blocks.37: Abu Talhah (RA) stood with a shield, shielding the Prophet {{1}} in front.
blocks.39: On the day of Uhud people moved away from the Prophet {{1}}, and Abu Talhah (RA) stood shielding the Prophet {{2}} in front with a shield. He was a skilled archer, drawing the bow hard. That day he broke two or three bows. When someone passed with a quiver, the Prophet {{3}} would say, pour it out for Abu Talhah (RA). When the Prophet {{4}} raised his head to look at the enemy, Abu Talhah (RA) would say, may my father and mother be sacrificed for you, do not raise your head, one of their arrows might hit you. My neck is in front of your neck.{{5}}
blocks.40: That day Anas (RA) saw two others as well. ‘A’ishah (RA) and Umm Sulaym (RA). Tucking up their garments, water-skins on their backs, they were running, pouring water into the mouths of the wounded. When the skin was empty they went back and refilled. The women were on the battlefield. In their hands not swords, but water-skins.{{1}}
blocks.41: Sa‘d ibn Abi Waqqas (RA) was shooting arrows in front of the Prophet {{1}}.
blocks.43: On the day of Uhud the Prophet {{1}} poured out his quiver for me and said, shoot, may my father and mother be sacrificed for you.{{2}}
blocks.44: ‘Ali (RA) used to say, I have not heard the Prophet {{1}} say ‘may my father and mother both be sacrificed’ for anyone except Sa‘d (RA). Sa‘d (RA) also saw, on the right and on the left of the Prophet {{2}}, two men in white clothes. Jibril and Mika’il (peace be upon them both). He had not seen them before or after.{{3}}
blocks.45: Umm ‘Umarah (RA), Nusaybah bint Ka‘b (RA), had come to the field that day first with a water-skin. As the Muslims broke, she came and stood in front of the Prophet {{1}}. She swung the sword, shot arrows. She received a deep wound on her shoulder. She struck Ibn Qami’ah many times, but he had two coats of mail on his body.{{2}}
blocks.46: Among these, some were a shield, some a water-skin, some a bow. Some offered their chest, some their back, some their hand. At home and at the office we too can stand beside someone. When someone falls into hardship and everyone moves away, staying is the greatest deed.
blocks.47: Meanwhile a man was roaming the field, an old oath in his throat. Ubayy ibn Khalaf. In Makkah he used to say to the Prophet {{1}}, I have a horse, named ‘Awd. Every day I feed him a lot. Riding on his back I will kill you. The Prophet {{2}} would say, God willing, I will kill you. On the day of Uhud he came covered in coat of mail and helmet and shouted, where is Muhammad? If he lives today I will not live. The Companions said, O Messenger of Allah, shall one of us go? The Prophet {{3}} said, let him come. When he came near the Prophet {{4}} took a small spear from the hand of al-Harith ibn al-Simmah (RA). The Companions say, with the spear in hand he gave such a shake that we scattered as insects fall off a camel’s back. Then he threw the spear at Ubayy’s throat, at the small gap between the helmet and coat of mail. With the blow he rolled off his horse. No blood came out, yet he was bellowing like a bull. His companions said, this is only a small scratch. He said, he had said in Makkah, I will kill you. By Allah, even if he had spat on me I would have died. On the road to Makkah, at a place called Sarif, he died.{{5}}
blocks.48: The man who wanted to make real on the battlefield the threat he had made sitting in Makkah was caught by his own threat.
blocks.50: The disbelievers began to go back. Abu Sufyan climbed the mountain and called out.
blocks.52: Abu Sufyan said, is Muhammad among the people? The Prophet {{1}} said, do not answer him. He said, is the son of Abu Quhafah among the people? He said, do not answer him. He said, is Ibn al-Khattab among the people? Then he said, these have all died, if they were alive they would have answered. ‘Umar (RA) could not hold himself. He said, you have lied, enemy of Allah! Allah has kept for you what will shame you.{{2}}
blocks.53: He called three names. As if he knew exactly that if these three remained, Islam would stand. The Prophet {{1}} told them to be silent. Because in that voice was a search, in the reply an address. But then when he shouted, Hubal is exalted! The Prophet {{2}} said, answer.
blocks.55: Abu Sufyan said, Hubal is exalted! The Prophet {{1}} said, answer him. They said, what shall we say? He said, say, Allah is the Most High, the Most Majestic. Abu Sufyan said, we have al-‘Uzza, and you have no ‘Uzza. The Prophet {{2}} said, answer him. They said, what shall we say? He said, say, Allah is our protector, and you have no protector. Abu Sufyan said, today is a repayment for the day of Badr, war is like buckets passing from hand to hand. You will find mutilation among your dead. I did not order it, but I did not dislike it either.{{3}}
blocks.56: There is a time to be silent, and a time to answer. Where answering would give away their location, silence. Where it is a matter of tawhid, everyone together, a declaration. We do exactly the opposite. In personal insult, ten minutes of shouting. In a question of religion, silence. Abu Sufyan called ‘Umar (RA) again. ‘Umar (RA) went near. He said, ‘Umar (RA), for Allah’s sake tell me, did we kill Muhammad? ‘Umar (RA) said, by Allah, no. He is listening to you right now. He said, you are more truthful to me than Ibn Qami’ah.{{1}}
blocks.57: Before leaving Abu Sufyan said, next year we meet on the field of Badr. The Prophet {{1}} said to one of the Companions, say, all right, this word remains between us and you. Then he sent ‘Ali (RA) after them. He said, see what they do. If they leave the horses beside them and ride camels, they are heading for Makkah. If they ride horses and drive camels, they are heading for Madinah. By the One in whose hand is my soul, if they go toward Madinah I will go, and fight them right there. ‘Ali (RA) returned and reported, they went riding camels with the horses beside them. Their faces are toward Makkah.{{2}}
blocks.59: Before Quraysh went back, some men and women went to the bodies of the Muslims. They cut noses, cut ears, ripped open bellies. Hind took Hamzah’s (RA) liver in her mouth. She wanted to chew it, could not swallow. She spat it out. She made necklaces and anklets out of the ears and noses of the Muslims.{{1}}
blocks.60: In the end she climbed a rock and sang: I have taken revenge for Badr, war after war. My insides are cooled. She got what she wanted. Yet she had to sing, had to say again and again, I am calm. The one who says after taking revenge, I am calm, has to say it again and again. Because peace has not actually come. The Prophet {{1}} finished tending the wounded at the camp, and set out to look for the dead after the battle. He found Hamzah’s (RA) body in the middle of the valley. Belly ripped open, nose and ears cut. The Prophet {{2}} stood. He said, I will never again be afflicted with a loss like you. I have never stood in a place of greater anger than this. He also said, Jibril informed me that it is written in the seven heavens, Hamzah ibn ‘Abd al-Muttalib is the lion of Allah, the lion of the Messenger of Allah.{{3}}
blocks.61: Then the Prophet {{1}} said, were it not that Safiyyah (RA) would be grieved, and that after me it would become a custom, I would leave him exactly like this, so that he would go into the bellies of beasts of prey and birds. If Allah ever grants me victory over Quraysh, I will mutilate thirty of them. The Companions said, by Allah, if we ever overcome them, we will mutilate in a way no Arab has ever done. In the fire of revenge the Companions too had made a promise. But the Prophet {{2}} forgave, was patient, and forbade mutilation. This was his rule.
blocks.63: The Messenger of Allah {{1}} used to urge us to give charity and forbid us from mutilation.{{2}}
blocks.64: He had the power to take revenge. He had feeling. A word had already come out of his mouth. Yet he stopped.{{1}}
blocks.65: In a fit of anger we too say such things. ‘I will teach such a lesson that it will be remembered for life’. It came out of the Prophet’s {{1}} mouth too. Then he took back his words.
blocks.66: Safiyyah bint ‘Abd al-Muttalib (RA) came running to Hamzah (RA), to see her brother. The Prophet {{1}} said to her son al-Zubayr (RA), go in front of your mother, turn her back, so she does not see her brother’s condition. Al-Zubayr (RA) went and said, mother, the Prophet {{2}} has told you to go back. Safiyyah (RA) said, why? I have heard that my brother has been mutilated. This is in the path of Allah. We are fully pleased with this. I will surely be patient and hope for the reward, God willing. Al-Zubayr (RA) informed the Prophet {{3}}. He said, let her go. Safiyyah (RA) went and saw her brother. She made du‘a. She recited Inna lillahi. She asked forgiveness.{{4}}
blocks.67: The mutilated body of her own brother. Yet patience. Because the brother had gone in the path of Allah. At news of death we break down, that is all right. Yet let us not deprive ourselves of these three: Inna lillahi, du‘a and istighfar.

quiz.q: After the tooth was broken, which verse was revealed about the Prophet ﷺ?
o: And Muhammad is only a messenger
Forgive them, pray for their forgiveness

quiz.q: To stop the bleeding of the Prophet’s ﷺ wound, what did Fatimah (RA) burn and apply as ash?
What lesson comes from the verse ‘You have no authority’?
o: The burden of judgment is Allah’s, not even the Prophet’s ﷺ
He had no authority to forgive
Responding to blows was forbidden to him
Even praying for the enemy was forbidden to him

quiz.q: The greatest anger at someone. Which verse of Uhud shows the way here?
o: ‘Do not think of them as dead’

quiz.q: How many wounds were found on the body of Anas ibn al-Nadr (RA)?
How did his sister recognize Anas ibn al-Nadr (RA)?
o: By a mole on his body
By the mark of a sword
By the tips of his fingers

quiz.q: Anas ibn al-Nadr’s (RA) words, ‘even without the Prophet ﷺ, I will remain for his religion’: what is the point?
o: One may leave the field on hearing a rumour
The fighting should have been stopped then
It was necessary to be sure the Prophet ﷺ had died
The religion does not stand on a person

quiz.q: Worship grew slack after the head of the family left. Which verse will you recall?
Whose hand went limp protecting the Prophet ﷺ on the day of Uhud?
Even though Talhah (RA) kept wanting to step forward saying ‘I, O Messenger of Allah’, why did the Prophet ﷺ stop him?
o: The men of the Ansar stepped forward first, one by one
Talhah (RA) had been seriously wounded by then
The Prophet ﷺ wanted to send him to the mountain
Talhah (RA) had gone to fetch a shield

quiz.q: When everyone leaves one person’s side, which Companions will you be like?
o: Those who left the pass and went down toward the spoils
Those who ran off toward Madinah
Those who threw away their weapons and sat down
Those who stayed around the Prophet ﷺ

quiz.q: Someone has made a great sacrifice for you. Which picture of Uhud will you remember?
o: Shielding with a shield in hand, running with a water-skin
Abu Sufyan’s call to the field of Badr

quiz.q: Where did Abu Sufyan say, before leaving, they would meet next year?
Whom did the Prophet ﷺ send to see which way Quraysh went?
Why did the Prophet ﷺ forbid answering Abu Sufyan’s call ‘Is Muhammad there?’
o: The Prophet ﷺ himself was wounded and unconscious
The Companions had all gone back to Madinah
The answer would have given away the Companions’ location
Abu Sufyan did not even want to hear the answer

quiz.q: To the call ‘Hubal is exalted!’ the Prophet ﷺ told them to answer, though to the earlier call he had told them to be silent. Why?
o: Here the enemy was ready to attack
Here the answer was not a location but a declaration of tawhid
Here the Companions were far greater in number

quiz.q: Whom did the Prophet ﷺ send to turn back Safiyyah (RA), who had come to see Hamzah (RA)?
What can be understood from Hind’s repeated singing ‘I am calm’ after the revenge?
o: Singing was her way to peace

quiz.q: Given Safiyyah’s (RA) grief and the fear of it ‘becoming a custom’, what did the Prophet ﷺ do about mutilation?
o: He ordered the mutilation of thirty
He immediately took thirty of Quraysh captive
He took back his words and forbade it
quiz.e: Ibn Ishaq ← Ibn Kathir; Sunan Abi Dawud 2667.

quiz.q: A brother has said words of revenge against a friend. What is the Prophet’s ﷺ example?
o: Mutilating thirty as the word said
Taking back what was said and forbidding it
Holding on to the declaration and waiting for a chance

porbos.title: Shrouds, Burial, and the Life of the Martyrs • The Women of Madinah • Out Again With Wounded Bodies • The Lesson Inside the Defeat • Final Word

blocks.0: Shrouds, Burial, and the Life of the Martyrs
blocks.1: Now the burial. About seventy bodies. All of them wounded, exhausted.
blocks.3: The Messenger of Allah {{1}} used to wrap two of the Uhud martyrs together in one cloth. Then he would say, which of these knew more of the Qur’an? When one was pointed out, he would lower that one into the grave first. And he would say, I am a witness over these on the Day of Resurrection. He ordered them buried with their blood. They were not washed, and the funeral prayer was not prayed over them.{{2}}
blocks.4: The memorizer of the Qur’an first. The one with more Qur’an in the chest is further ahead before Allah. For some, no shroud could be found. Mus‘ab ibn ‘Umayr (RA), who had been the happiest young man in Makkah.
blocks.6: We migrated with the Messenger of Allah {{1}} seeking the pleasure of Allah. Our reward is certain with Allah. Some of us have passed on without enjoying anything of this world. Mus‘ab ibn ‘Umayr (RA) is one of them. He was martyred on the day of Uhud. He left nothing but one namirah. If we covered his head, his feet came out; if we covered his feet, his head. The Prophet {{2}} said, cover his head, and put idhkhir grass over his feet.{{3}}
blocks.7: One day food was brought before ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Awf (RA). He was fasting. He said, Mus‘ab (RA) died, and he was better than I. He had to be shrouded in one sheet, if the head was covered the feet came out. Hamzah (RA) also died, and he too was better than I. Then the world was opened up before us. I fear that the reward for our good deeds has been given in advance. Then he began to weep, and left the food untouched.{{1}}
blocks.8: Jabir’s (RA) father ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr ibn Haram (RA) was also a martyr. Jabir (RA) was removing the cloth from his father’s face and weeping. The Companions wanted to stop him. The Prophet {{1}} did not stop him. He said, whether you weep or not, the angels were shading him with their wings, until he was lifted away.{{2}}
blocks.9: ‘Amr ibn al-Jamuh (RA) was lame. He had four sons, like lions. They said, father, you have an excuse, do not go. He went to the Prophet {{1}} and said, O Messenger of Allah, I hope to set foot in Paradise with this very lame foot of mine. The Prophet {{2}} said, you have an excuse, jihad is not obligatory on you. To his sons he said, do not stop him, perhaps Allah will grant him martyrdom. He went, and was martyred.{{3}}
blocks.11: A man said to the Prophet {{1}} on the day of Uhud, tell me, if I am killed, where will I be? He said, in Paradise. He threw away the dates in his hand, then fought, and was killed.{{2}}
blocks.12: The moment of throwing away the dates is the real one. When one gets the assurance of Paradise, even the last meal on earth feels like a burden. Another, Usayrim, ‘Amr ibn Thabit. He did not want to come to Islam. On the morning of Uhud he suddenly accepted Islam, went down onto the field with a sword in hand, and was wounded fighting. His tribesmen found him and asked, why have you come? For the tribe’s sake, or for Islam? He said, for Islam. I believed in Allah and His Messenger, then I fought alongside the Prophet {{1}}. A little later he died. The Prophet {{2}} said, he is of Paradise. Abu Hurayrah (RA) used to say, tell me, a man of Paradise who never prayed a single prayer? When people did not recognize him he would say, Usayrim. Another, Quzman. On the field he alone killed seven or eight men. He was wounded. The people said, today you became a hero, take the good news. He said, what good news? I fought only for the honour of my people. When the pain grew he finished himself with his own arrow. When he was mentioned, the Prophet {{3}} used to say, he is of Hell.{{4}}
blocks.13: One accepted Islam in the morning, not even one prayer’s time had come, a martyr by evening. Another killed seven or eight, but for his people. A deed is one thing. Intention is another. In our homes, in the work of religion, in the work of society too, the question arises: for whom am I doing this? People will praise me, is that it?
blocks.16: Never think of those who have been killed in the way of Allah as dead; rather they are alive. They are given provision from their Lord. They rejoice in whatever Allah has given them out of His bounty.{{1}}
blocks.17: One day Masruq asked ‘Abdullah ibn Mas‘ud (RA) about this verse.
blocks.19: We asked ‘Abdullah about this verse. He said, we asked the Messenger of Allah {{1}} about it. He said, their souls are in the bellies of green birds. They have lamps hanging from the Throne. They roam in Paradise wherever they wish, then return to those lamps. Their Lord looked upon them and said, do you want anything? They said, what more could we want? We are roaming in Paradise wherever we wish. Three times the same question. When they understood that they would not be left alone unless they asked, they said, our Lord, we want our souls returned to our bodies, so that we may be killed again in Your way. When He saw they had no further wish, He left them.{{2}}
blocks.20: Even after getting everything in Paradise, their one wish: to die again in the way of Allah. Eight years later the Prophet {{1}} came to Uhud.
blocks.22: The Messenger of Allah {{1}} prayed over the martyrs of Uhud, after eight years, as if bidding farewell to the living and the dead. Then he went up on the pulpit. He said, I am going ahead of you, I am a witness over you. The place of your meeting with me is the Hawd. I can see it from here. I do not fear shirk for you. I fear that you will compete over the world. ‘Uqbah says, this was my last sight of the Messenger of Allah {{2}}.{{3}}
blocks.23: Competing over the world. The fear that, even eight years later, standing before the martyrs, was in the Prophet’s {{1}} heart. Let us look at our own homes. What is our competition today?
blocks.25: Everyone was returning along the road to Madinah. By the roadside women were standing. A woman of Banu Dinar had lost her husband, brother and father as martyrs at Uhud. She was told. She asked, how is the Messenger of Allah {{1}}? It was said, well, as you wish. She said, show me, I will see for myself. He was pointed out. She looked and said, you are alive, so every misfortune after this is trivial.{{2}}
blocks.26: Husband gone, brother gone, father gone. Yet she asked first, how is the Prophet {{1}}? Returning home the Prophet {{2}} gave his own sword to his daughter Fatimah (RA). He said, daughter, wash the blood from this. By Allah, today it kept its word for me. ‘Ali (RA) also gave his sword. The Prophet {{3}} said, if you fought well, Sahl ibn Hunayf (RA) and Abu Dujanah (RA) also fought well.{{4}}
blocks.27: Not praise of himself. The Prophet {{1}} said to ‘Ali (RA), others also fought well. At the end of a task do we even name our colleagues? Passing by the house of Banu ‘Abd al-Ashhal, the Prophet {{2}} heard the sound of weeping.
blocks.29: The Messenger of Allah {{1}} returned from Uhud. The women of the Ansar were weeping for their slain husbands. He said, but for Hamzah (RA) there is no one to weep. Then he fell asleep. Waking, he heard them weeping. He said, today they are weeping for Hamzah (RA).{{2}}
blocks.30: Sa‘d ibn Mu‘adh (RA) and Usayd ibn al-Hudayr (RA) said to the women of their houses, first weep for the uncle of the Prophet {{1}}. They came, weeping. The Prophet {{2}} said to them, go back, may Allah have mercy on you, you yourselves have already offered condolence. And from that day he forbade wailing aloud.{{3}}
blocks.31: The house with no one to weep, the Prophet {{1}} remembered that house first. Around us there is someone for whom there is no one to weep. A sick old person, a migrant worker, a child in an orphanage. How many of us remember them?
blocks.33: The night after Uhud was one of terrible anxiety. Would the enemy not return? The Prophet’s {{1}} fear was elsewhere. If Quraysh thought on the road, we did not win, we came back without finishing, then they would come back and attack Madinah.
blocks.35: When that blow struck the Messenger of Allah {{1}}, and the polytheists withdrew, he feared they would return. He said, who will go after them? Seventy responded, among them Abu Bakr (RA) and al-Zubayr (RA).{{2}}
blocks.36: The next morning an announcement: the enemy must be pursued. Only those who had been in yesterday’s battle could go. Jabir (RA) said, O Messenger of Allah, I want to go with you. My father left my sisters in my charge, so I could not go to Uhud. The Prophet {{1}} gave him permission. Two brothers of Banu ‘Abd al-Ashhal. Both injured. No horse. One less hurt than the other. When his brother could no longer walk, he put him on his shoulder. A little way, then he walked again. In this way they reached the Muslims.{{2}}
blocks.38: Those who responded obediently to the call of Allah and the Messenger even after being wounded, for such righteous and God-fearing ones there is a great reward.{{1}}
blocks.39: Even after being wounded. Body broken, clothes soaked in blood, no horse. Yet hearing the call, setting out. The wounded brother on the shoulder of the less wounded brother. Even when the body stops, the heart does not. To be able to return to work even after losing, this is the real strength. At Hamra’ al-Asad, eight miles away, they pitched camp. Ma‘bad ibn Abi Ma‘bad al-Khuza‘i was passing that way. Still a polytheist. But there was friendship between the Khuza‘ah tribe and the Prophet {{1}}. He came and said, Muhammad, we are grieved by the misfortune that has befallen you and your companions. We wish that Allah keep you safe. Ma‘bad went to Abu Sufyan. At al-Rawha’ Quraysh were sitting then, thinking, let us go back and finish them off. Ma‘bad said, Muhammad is coming with an army the like of which I have never seen. Even those who were not there yesterday have come, burning with rage. Abu Sufyan stopped.{{2}}
blocks.40: The Prophet {{1}} stayed there Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday. Then he returned to Madinah. On the way back Abu ‘Izzah was caught, that poet who had been released at Badr. He had come again on behalf of Quraysh. He said, Muhammad, let me go. The Prophet {{2}} said, no. You will go to Makkah, stroke your cheeks and say, I fooled Muhammad twice, this will not be. After letting one go once, if the same man does the same thing again, there is no room left for mercy. The order was given for his execution.{{3}}
blocks.41: Mercy is good. But against the one who turns that mercy into an opportunity, resolve is also needed.
blocks.43: Uhud was neither a complete victory nor a complete defeat. Seventy were martyred, yet Quraysh did not dare enter Madinah. In Surah Al ‘Imran the Qur’an has described every stage of the battle, what happened, why it happened. The first point: Allah had fulfilled His promise.
blocks.45: Allah fulfilled His promise at that time, when by His command you were killing the enemies, until you showed weakness and disagreed among yourselves about the command, and when Allah showed you what you love, you disobeyed (your commander). Among you were some who desired this world and some who desired the Hereafter. Then Allah turned you away from them, so that He might test you. Yet He has forgiven you. Allah is most gracious to the believers.{{1}}
blocks.46: In the beginning the Companions were winning the fight. Then a mistake, then loss. But at the end it is written: Yet He has forgiven you. There were two mistakes: weakness and disobeying the commander’s order. The cause was one: the thing they loved, that is, the spoils. And this loss was not a punishment. It was a test and a correction. The way a father disciplines a son, a teacher a student.{{1}}
blocks.47: The hardest part: those who had made the mistake, the Prophet {{1}} was then calling them from behind.
blocks.49: (Recall that time) when you were running up in panic and not looking back at anyone, while the Messenger was calling you from behind. So Allah gave you grief in place of (giving the Messenger) grief, so that you would not grieve in future, neither over what slipped out of your hands, nor over any other misfortune that may befall you. Allah is fully aware of what you do.{{1}}
blocks.50: The Messenger was calling from behind, and no one turned to look. For the sake of hearing whose call they had endured so much, they could not even respond to that call. Because then there was fear in their eyes. And in fear, the ears too close. Yet in response to that mistake, it is hard to imagine anything gentler than what was said.
blocks.52: (O Prophet!) After these events, it was Allah’s mercy that made you gentle with the people. Had you been harsh and hard-hearted, they would have dispersed from around you. So forgive them, pray for their forgiveness, and keep consulting them in important matters. Then when you have made up your mind and resolved on a matter, rely on Allah. Surely Allah loves those who rely on Him.{{1}}
blocks.53: About those who had fled, the language of the verse: forgive them, pray for their forgiveness, keep consulting them. There is no word to stop consulting. After a mistake the door of consultation is more open. Whom we trust, the moment they err once, we take that trust back. When a child errs once, the father says, I will not give you any responsibility again. Allah said to His Prophet, you were gentle, so they are there. Had you not been gentle, everyone would have gone away. Another point:
blocks.55: When you were struck by a calamity, twice the like of which you had inflicted (on the enemies), do you say, where did this calamity come from? Say, it is from yourselves. Surely Allah has power over all things.{{1}}
blocks.56: Where did the calamity come from? From ourselves. As Badr’s victory was Allah’s help, so Uhud’s loss was the fruit of our own mistake. To be able to say these two things together is the maturity of faith. We call success our own ability, failure someone else’s fault. Or leave failure to fate. Uhud taught us to stand before failure and say: this has come from ourselves.{{1}}
blocks.57: The Qur’an did not hide the Companions’ mistake. Nor did it hide, beside that mistake, the announcement of Allah’s forgiveness. Among those who had fled was ‘Uthman ibn ‘Affan (RA). Ibn ‘Umar (RA) said later, I know of his turning back on the day of Uhud. I bear witness that Allah has forgiven him.{{1}}
blocks.59: Some pictures remain from this dars of Uhud. A sword whose right has to be asked for. A Wahshi, who later came into Islam, and to whom the Prophet {{1}} said, keep your face away from me. A Hanzalah, whom the angels washed. Fifty archers, who withdrew from the command on the strength of one argument.
blocks.60: A Prophet {{1}} whose tooth broke, whose face filled with blood, and to whom Allah said, you have no authority. An Anas ibn al-Nadr (RA), who said, even if the Prophet {{2}} is not there, I will remain for his religion. A Safiyyah (RA), whose brother’s body was mutilated, yet who said, I will be patient.
blocks.61: And the greatest point is not in Talhah’s (RA) hand, not in Sa‘d’s (RA) arrows. It is in Allah’s forgiveness: Yet He has forgiven you. So take one task with you from today’s dars.
blocks.63: His tooth broken, his face wet with blood, yet the Prophet {{1}} left the burden of judgment in Allah’s hands; and Allah forgave the Companions who had fled in error. Today I will ask myself one question: the person I am most angry with, have I been able to leave the burden of judging them in Allah’s hands?
blocks.64: Today I will quietly pray once for good for them; this small deed I will not give up from today on.

A rule that a poet should never be punished
quiz.e: Ibn Ishaq ← Ibn Kathir; Sahih al-Bukhari 6133.

quiz.q: You are wounded and tired, yet the call to work came. Which incident of Uhud will you remember?
o: The Jews’ argument about Saturday through Mukhayriq
Ibn Ubayy turning back with three hundred men
The two wounded brothers going to Hamra’ al-Asad
Abu Sufyan’s promise of the field of Badr

quiz.q: From ‘the Messenger was calling from behind’ in Surah Al ‘Imran 3:153, what can be understood?
o: The Prophet ﷺ himself was then fleeing the field
In fear a person cannot hear even the call of a loved one
The call was made only to the Ansar
Everyone returned at once on hearing the call

quiz.q: According to Surah Al ‘Imran 3:159, what was the Prophet ﷺ told to do with the Companions who erred?
o: Leave their company and find new companions
Stop their consultation and decide everything himself
Rule harshly and straighten everyone out

quiz.q: What is the lesson of the words ‘it is from yourselves’ in Surah Al ‘Imran 3:165?
o: Regarding failure as the path to success
Looking for one’s own mistake in failure

quiz.q: A responsible person made a mistake. According to 3:159, what treatment is appropriate?
o: Never giving them any responsibility again
Humiliating them before everyone with strict discipline
Keeping open the door of forgiveness, prayer and consultation

quiz.q: After doing badly in an exam, a student blames the teacher. Which saying of Uhud is for them?
Though success and failure both come by Allah’s will, what is it the maturity of faith to say in the face of failure?
o: ‘It is written in fate, nothing can be done’
‘The leader had taken the wrong decision’

quiz.q: As the opposite of withdrawing trust from someone after a single mistake, which scene fits?
o: Not taking Ibn Ubayy along to Hamra’ al-Asad
Sending the young back from the battle
Continuing consultation with the Companions who erred
